messages:
Grace L: Heads-up — PM asked for a way for customers to temporarily unmask request payloads for legal/partner review. We can’t show raw by default. Proposal: `deferred redaction` — encrypt raw verbatim at ingest with customer KMS, keep scrubbed copy in telemetry, enable breakglass unmask that requires justification + audit + TTL. What do folks think about telemetry, quotas, and console UX?

Sanjay P: I like the idea, but 2 immediate concerns: storage cost for encrypted raw and how we account for it against customer quota. If raw is encrypted and never revealed, do we charge full ingest tokens?

Evan M: For quotas I’d argue charge on scrubbed size for normal ops, but log a separate "raw_retention" metric for billing. We should be explicit in API terms. Also need to consider sampling: if we sample requests for telemetry, do we sample both scrubbed and encrypted raw consistently?

Carmen R: Important: sampling bias. If breakglass requests come from rare error cases, we’ll disproportionately need raw retention for those paths. Need to advertise/monitor tail retention. Dashboard should surface estimated retained bytes per route so customers can understand costs.

Julie K: Console UX note — customers want a single knob to toggle temporary unmask per route, but also per-tenant RBAC for who can trigger. UX should show audit entries inline (who requested, reason, TTL). We should avoid a global ON/OFF that gives false security.

Evan M: On implementation: ingest pipeline could do: 1) apply schema-driven redaction to produce scrubbed_payload 2) encrypt original -> store in S3 with envelope key scoped to tenant 3) attach pointer to scrubbed log entry. Breakglass flow decrypts only after auth + audit record. Example schema snippet: ```json
{"route": "/chat/gen", "fields": {"user.email": "redact", "user.name": "pseudonymize:sha256", "attachments": "strip"}}
```
This allows per-route rules and avoids heuristic PII at runtime.

Sanjay P: Schema-driven rules are great but we need a fallback heuristic. Many customers won't submit exhaustive schemas. Maybe default to "safe-mode" that strips strings that look like emails/SSNs and hashes long tokens.

Carmen R: Telemetry: we must emit metrics for: ingest_bytes_scrubbed, ingest_bytes_raw_encrypted, retained_raw_count, unmask_actions_count, unmask_latency. Dashboards should show sampled vs full rates. Also surface sample probability per route so SRE can adjust.

Grace L: Agree. Also the rollout plan: start as an opt-in feature behind a console preview toggle for a handful of tenants (canary), log any unmask attempts to a high-fidelity audit sink, and require legal approval for early adopters.

Evan M: About sampling: if console shows errors based on sampled logs, they might miss issues that only appear in un-sampled raws. Suggest adding a "canary full-capture" mode that captures raw for a tiny percent of requests (0.1%) to validate redaction heuristics and detect regressions.

Julie K: From RBAC side, key points: separate permission to request unmask + separate permission to approve. Approvals should be time-limited and require justification text. Console should snapshot the scrubbing diff so approvers see what would change when raw is revealed.

Sanjay P: One more internal API debate: do we change the public request API to return a pointer to scrubbed vs raw? I prefer we keep API unchanged and expose telemetry/console-only pointers so client libraries are not impacted. Any objections?

Carmen R: Keep API stable. Console-only controls are safer. But we must version the telemetry schema so analytics consumers can join on route + sample flags. Include a sample_key hash in logs so sampled vs unsampled grouping is deterministic.

ops-bot: Deploybot: canary rollout configured for feature "deferred-redaction" -> stage: preview -> targets: tenant-set A -> started at 2026-03-21T16:05:22Z

Evan M: Quick nit: breakglass TTL should be short (default 1 hour) and we should support ephemeral reveal tokens that expire. Also encrypt raw with a key that supports re-encrypt-on-demand for customer KMS rotation.

Grace L: Action items I’ll take: 1) draft an RFC with storage/billing model (charge scrubbed-bytes + small retention fee for encrypted raw) 2) sample dashboard mock that shows retained bytes per route and unmask audit panel 3) canary plan and privacy checklist for legal.

Sanjay P: I’ll prototype schema-driven redactor and a fallback safe-mode heuristic.

Carmen R: I’ll add telemetry counters and a dashboard spec.

Julie K: I’ll wire up RBAC and approval UX flows.

Grace L: Thanks — if nobody objects I’ll start the RFC and tag legal/security for review.

Evan M: No objections from me. Fast follow: add a short experiment to capture 0.1% full raw for 2 weeks to evaluate heuristics.

Carmen R: +1 on experiment.

Julie K: +1

Grace L: Great — filing RFC now and will ping this thread when draft is up.
